coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Rich Sorro Commons
record.summary: Rich Sorro Commons is a 100-unit affordable housing building at 150 Berry St in Mission Bay for families and people living with HIV/AIDS, with a project page on Mission Housing's website (the organisation calls itself 'the community's affordable housing developer since 1971'; the page does not say in so many words that it developed this building). That page states the building opened in July 2002, the first affordable family housing development in Mission Bay. The page and DBI's permit give 100 units; the Assessor's roll for the residential lot records 101.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL lot geometry -- the outline is the union of Assessor lots 8706264 and 8706003 (6,453 m2, active), so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a surveyed building footprint: it includes any yard, setback or plaza inside the lot and can sit a little off the walls. Until 2026-10-12 this record showed the surveyed building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints (mblr SF8706264)); 95% of that outline lies inside the lot and it covered 69% of the lot. The building spans two Assessor lots, 8706264 and 8706003, which DataSF's parcel layer lists on Berry St (8706264 as 150 Berry St, 8706003 as 150-152 Berry St). The Assessor's secured roll puts the building's data under lot 8706003 (150 Berry St, Multi-Family Residential, 101 units, year built 2002); the roll's entry for lot 8706264 is for 213 King St (Commercial Retail, no units, year built 2003), so the roll does not cite lot 8706264 for this building.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lots 8706264 and 8706003 (mapped 2001-03-20, 2003-08-27; active), joined into one outline; the earlier outline came from: DataSF Building Footprints (mblr SF8706264); name/address from Mission Housing's own project page and press coverage; OpenStreetMap way 679290110 tags the footprint but carries no name/address of its own

Notes on pages that could not be read are now plain statements, and mapping-process detail is left to the shape's own notes. No change to the record's status or shape.
Rich Sorro Commons now uses its Assessor lot lines.

The Rich Sorro Commons page no longer says the Assessor's year built is 2003: that year belongs to a retail lot at 213 King St. The roll entry for 150 Berry St, under lot 8706003, gives 2002 and 101 units, matching the July 2002 opening.

The map notes for Rich Sorro Commons said 101 units, 174,100 square feet, a supportive housing building and a Head Start centre at 152 Berry St. Mission Housing's project page and the DBI permit both say 100 units; the page gives 158,000 square feet, serves families and people with AIDS/HIV, and mentions only 'a childcare center'. A dated correction was recorded, and the summary already said 100 units. open_questions: The DataSF Assessor's secured roll for 150 Berry St (lot 8706003: Multi-Family Residential, 101 units, year_property_built 2002) agrees with Mission Housing's stated July 2002 opening, and gives 101 units where Mission Housing and the permit say 100. The record had earlier read a 2003 year built from lot 8706264, but the roll lists that lot at 213 King St (Commercial Retail, no units, year built 2003), a different property, so that year is not used.

The 2000 construction permit's own block/lot (block 3795B, lot 001, an older pre-redevelopment block grid) differs from the Assessor's current lot for 150 Berry St (parcel 8706003); the address, 100-unit/5-story description, and October 2002 permit-completion date (DBI: completed 2002-10-21; Mission Housing states a July 2002 opening and the Assessor gives 2002 as year built for lot 8706003) line up with this building, so this is treated as Mission Bay's redevelopment-era block renumbering, not a different building. No source read states the renumbering.
